description: Deterministic detector rules (SPEC §2.10), implemented in Go (reference) and TypeScript and pinned by contracts/vectors/detectors. Patterns are RE2- and ECMAScript-compatible, with no lookaround, no backreferences and no inline flags; flags are passed separately (Go compiles "(?flags)" + pattern when flags is non-empty, JS compiles new RegExp(pattern, flags + "g")). Where the SPEC writes \s, these files write [\t\n\f\r ], which is exactly RE2's \s, so both engines match the same text. Offsets in findings are UTF-16 code units, half-open.

reference_text.description: The reference for numbers, dates, URLs and quotes: the text of every pre-packing, pre-dedup evidence item except untrusted ones, user_request, system_instructions, and every value of rules. Each part is scanned on its own, so a token never spans two parts; for quotes the normalized parts are joined with "\n".

text_normalization.description: Used by quotes_not_in_evidence and system_prompt_leak: map curly quotes to straight ones, lowercase ASCII letters only (A-Z), collapse every whitespace run to one space, trim. Works on code points.

normalize.description: Remove every "," and "%", then remove a trailing zero fraction (1,299.00 -> 1299, 30% -> 30, 4.50 stays 4.50).

skip_list_markers.description: A response number that starts inside a match of this pattern is a list marker and is skipped.

small_integers.description: A response number whose normalized form has no "." and whose value is <= min_integer is skipped, unless its raw token ends in "%", the code unit just before it is one of currency_prefix, or one of the next window_tokens matches of window_token after it matches unit (case-insensitive).

numbers_not_in_evidence.fires_when: Some response number that is not skipped has a normalized form that is not in the set of normalized numbers found in the reference text (no skips apply to the reference).
numbers_not_in_evidence.finding: The raw number token as it appears in the response.

dates_not_in_evidence.overlap: Patterns are applied in the order listed; a match that overlaps a date already found in the same text is ignored (so "15 March 2026" is one date, not also "March 2026").
dates_not_in_evidence.normalize: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM for month_year, zero-padded. A match whose month is not 1-12 or whose day is not 1-31 is ignored.
dates_not_in_evidence.fires_when: Some response date is known neither exactly nor by prefix: a response YYYY-MM-DD needs the same date in the reference; a response YYYY-MM needs a reference date equal to it or starting with it plus "-".
dates_not_in_evidence.finding: The raw date text as it appears in the response.

normalize.description: Repeatedly strip a trailing character in strip_trailing, then lowercase the scheme and the authority (the text between "://" and the first "/", "?" or "#").

urls_not_in_evidence.fires_when: Some normalized response URL is not in the set of normalized URLs found in the reference text.
urls_not_in_evidence.finding: The response URL after trailing characters are stripped (original case).

quotes_not_in_evidence.normalize: text_normalization, then strip leading and trailing characters in strip_edges.
quotes_not_in_evidence.fires_when: Some quote (capture group 1) with at least min_words whitespace-separated words after normalization is not a substring of the normalized reference text.
quotes_not_in_evidence.finding: The text between the quote marks.

citation_out_of_range.fires_when: Some citation number n is 0 or greater than max(highest [Document N] / [Doc N] / [Source N] marker number in the extracted evidence, number of evidence items before dedup).

secret_pattern.fires_when: Some pattern match in the response does not occur verbatim in user_request.
secret_pattern.finding: The span of the match; the matched text itself must be masked before it is stored or displayed.

system_prompt_leak.fires_when: After text_normalization of system_instructions (S) and the response (R), S has at least min_code_points code points and some window S[i, i+200) with i = 0, 50, 100, ... plus the final window S[len-200, len) occurs in R. Implementations use a rolling hash over R's 200-code-point windows and confirm every hash hit by comparing the text.
system_prompt_leak.finding: Unaligned (start and end -1): offsets refer to normalized text.
